comments.content: The window-controls inset is duplicated as magic numbers in three rules (138px here, 142px below for `.main--aside-hidden .main__top` / `.rp-chrome`). These must stay in sync with the actual control geometry defined elsewhere; if the control size changes, title bars silently overlap or leave a gap. Extract a shared token (e.g. `--window-controls-width: 138px`) and express the second rule as `calc(var(--window-controls-width) + 4px)`.

`.stall-banner--soft` is declared **before** `.stall-banner`, and both selectors have the same specificity (0,1,0). Because `MainNotices.tsx` always renders the element with `class="stall-banner error-banner stall-banner--soft"`, the later base rules (`.stall-banner` and `.stall-banner.error-banner`, which re-set `background`/`border`) win the cascade, so this modifier has **no visual effect at all** — the “soft warning” tint is silently lost. Move the modifier after the base rule (or raise its specificity, e.g. `.stall-banner.stall-banner--soft`).

Transitioning `right` animates a layout property: every frame invalidates layout for the whole overlay subtree (composer card, textarea, chips) and forces re-layout of the transcript underneath while the side panel is being toggled. Prefer a composited property (`transform: translateX()` / `translate`) driven by the same state. The identical `transition: right ...` also exists in `.ask-user-wrap`.

`outline: none` removes the only focus indicator of the find-bar input, and no replacement (`:focus-visible` / `:focus-within`) is provided anywhere for `.chat-find`. Keyboard users tabbing into the in-conversation find bar get no visible focus. Add an explicit indicator on the container so it stays visible even when the input borderless.

Same pattern as the find bar: `outline: none` leaves only a subtle border-color change (`--border-subtle` → `--border-strong`, both 1px) as focus feedback on the ask-user textarea, which is hard to perceive. Add a focus ring (or restore the outline for `:focus-visible`).

The `!important` reset is guarded by a hard-coded negation list of chip classes. Any new inline markup class added later (e.g. a new mention/chip component) is silently force-stripped (`font`, `color`, `background`, `text-decoration` all `!important`) and can only be fixed by remembering to extend this selector. Consider whitelisting with a single marker attribute/class (e.g. `.composer__input [data-rich]`) so the reset applies to everything *except* marked content.

comments.content: `.ext-field-hint` is defined twice with conflicting intent. This first block sets `display: block; margin-top: 4px; font-size: 11.5px`, but the later rule (around line ~1402) re-declares the same selector with `margin: 0; padding: 6px 14px 10px; font-size: 12px`. Since the later rule wins, `margin-top: 4px` here is dead code and the two rules disagree on the hint's font size/spacing, which makes the rendered layout depend on source order. Keep a single definition (the block-scoped one with padding) and delete this one, or rename one of them so the intent is explicit.

`.summary-panel__active-agents` is declared twice back-to-back; the second rule only adds `flex: 1`. Splitting a single element's declarations across two identical selectors makes the layout harder to follow and invites divergence on future edits — merge `flex: 1` into the first block.

This block correctly disables the transition and the summary-panel entrance animation under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, but the continuously running keyframe animations in this file are not covered — `.rp-traj__spin` (0.9s linear infinite) and `.summary-panel__spin` (0.9s linear infinite) keep spinning. Note that `tokens.css` only zeroes `--motion-*` durations, and there is no global animation kill switch, so these infinite rotations remain for motion-sensitive users. The project already establishes the pattern of disabling animation per-selector (e.g. `.ext-skeleton__bar` in app-foundation.css); extend it here, keeping only the animation removal so the status icon still conveys state.

The comment above promises the placeholder never paints over typed glyphs, but the `z-index: 1` override only matches when `.composer__input` is a **direct child** of `.composer-editor-wrap`. If the editor is wrapped in an intermediate element (or the wrapper class is applied to a container holding a toolbar/fragment), the child combinator fails and the editor keeps the default stacking, so the absolutely positioned `.composer-editor__placeholder` (z-index: 0) can render above typed text. Prefer a descendant selector so the guarantee holds regardless of intermediate markup.

This block is declared after the `max-width: 680px` and `max-width: 460px` blocks, and it has the same specificity (`.settings-page__main`, 0-1-0) while setting the `padding` shorthand. Source order therefore makes it win for non-mac at ≤680px/≤460px: the 72px bottom inset and 14px side insets defined for narrow screens are discarded (and the 460px horizontal padding is overridden too), while `.platform-mac .settings-page__main` (0-2-0) keeps them — so mac and non-mac render different padding at the same width. Move this rule before the 680px block (or merge it into the existing blocks).

comments.content:
The document root hardcodes both `lang="zh-CN"` and `data-theme="dark"`, but the app resolves locale/theme at runtime (`src/hooks/useAppSettings.ts:91` sets `documentElement.lang`, `src/main.tsx:33-35` sets `data-theme` after the module executes).

Consequences:
1. Theme: for users whose persisted preference is `light`/`system` (light), the first paint is rendered with the dark token set, producing a visible dark flash (the main window is also `transparent: true`, which makes the flash more noticeable). Because the entry script is `type="module"` (deferred), it runs after the initial render opportunity, so simply setting the attribute a bit earlier inside main.tsx is not enough.
2. Locale: assistive technologies read the page as Chinese until settings load, so non-`zh-CN` users briefly get the wrong language announcement.

Suggest adding a tiny inline (non-deferred) bootstrap script in `<head>` that reads the same persisted keys used by `loadThemePreference`/`loadSkin` before the first paint, and keeping the static attributes only as a fallback. Also confirm the hardcoded `zh-CN` still matches the declared default locale in the i18n setup.

<html lang="zh-CN" data-theme="dark">
    <!-- Pre-paint bootstrap: must run before CSS/paint, keep in sync with src/lib/theme.ts -->
    <script>
      (function () {
        try {
          var p = localStorage.getItem("keencode.theme");
          var t = p === "light" || p === "dark" ? p : null;
          if (!t) {
            t = window.matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: light)").matches
              ? "light"
              : "dark";
          }
          document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", t);
        } catch (e) {
          /* keep the static default */
        }
      })();
    </script>

If the process ignores SIGTERM (or the kill/exit race is lost), the awaited `sample()` never settles and the entire benchmark hangs forever with no diagnostic. When the regex fails to match (e.g. the workflow is reformatted, the step id changes, or the `build:` job is reordered/renamed), `undefined.replace` throws a bare `TypeError` **before** `assert.ok(script, ...)` runs, so the intended diagnostic never fires and the failure is opaque. In addition, the pattern is tightly coupled to exact YAML shape (`id: release` newline, `run: |` newline, capture terminated by a literal `\n  build:`) and the dedent assumes the step body is indented with exactly 10 spaces; any indentation change silently captures a truncated/wrong script instead of failing loudly. Assert on the match first and derive the dedent from the captured indentation.

comments.content: The encode/decode dual role of the initialize DTO in crates/keencode-acp/src/capability.rs yields inconsistent serde tolerance: `delete` is required while the surrounding `session_capabilities` is `#[serde(default)]`. On decode, a peer that predates the `delete` supplement (or omits `agentCapabilities.sessionCapabilities`) either has a valid response rejected as `InvalidResponse` (`missing field delete`) or has undeclared support silently upgraded to `SessionDeleteCapabilities::default()`. Add `#[serde(default)]` to `delete` for compatibility, and on the decode side use `Option<InitializeSessionCapabilitiesDto>` (or a dedicated decode view) to preserve the undeclared semantics instead of fabricating a default.

comments.content: The `0` exhaustion sentinel in crates/keencode-acp/src/sequence.rs is fragile in three places: `peek()` leaks it (`0` is never a valid sequence, so a caller previewing/persisting the next sequence emits an invalid value), the `if next == 0` guard in the restore path is unreachable because `checked_add` only fails on overflow, and `checked_add(1).unwrap_or(0)` silently maps overflow to the magic `0` without documenting the convention on the field. Express exhaustion in the type (`Option<u64>`, `NonZeroU64`, or an explicit `exhausted` flag) so callers must handle it; if the sentinel is kept, document it on the field and replace the dead guard with a real watermark bound check.

comments.content: Root-vs-subagent phase is inferred from the string literal `"root"`, which is only one of the two root identities the codebase supports. `Collaboration::register_root` / `prospective_root_agent_id` allocate roots with namespaced ids (`root/{namespace}/{sequence}`), and `collaboration.rs` explicitly accepts both that form and the literal `"root"` when validating recovered roots (see `root_agent_id_belongs_to_namespace(&..) && ..as_str() != "root"`). Such a namespaced root turn would therefore be reported to hooks as `SubagentStart` instead of `UserPromptSubmit`, and the special `hook_prompt_blocked` error would be mapped to `TurnStartAbortReason::Failed` instead of `PromptBlocked` (so prompt-blocked cleanup semantics are lost). Prefer an explicit phase/flag on `TurnStartHookContext` instead of inferring it from an id, or at least also accept the namespaced root form (`child agents are `agent-{uuid}`, so the `root/` prefix cannot collide).

Cancellation observed while this call is still waiting for `circuit.entrance` permanently opens the circuit, even though this call has not spawned any worker yet (the worker currently holding the entrance belongs to a different, concurrent call and manages its own state). Because `HookCircuitStore` shares one circuit per hook across all turns of a declaration generation, a single transient turn cancellation permanently disables the hook for every later turn (`CircuitOpen` on every subsequent invocation) until the hook declaration changes. `PermanentlyOpen` is documented as covering cases where a residual worker may exist; here it does not. Consider only returning `Cancelled` on this path (no worker to strand), and reserve `open_permanently()` for the post-spawn cancellation/timeout paths.

`char::is_alphanumeric()` is Unicode-aware, so hook names containing non-ASCII letters/digits (CJK, Cyrillic, full-width forms, homoglyphs) pass registration, contradicting the documented contract ("letters, digits and `-_.:/`"). These frozen names are embedded in logs and in the injected hook-context boundary text (`hook_context_text`), where confusable characters can misattribute context to a look-alike hook. comments.content: `TH32CS_SNAPTHREAD` with a pid of `0` snapshots the threads of the **entire system**, and the loop resumes the first thread whose owner pid matches the child. On Windows the child is only guaranteed to have exactly one thread while it is still suspended; if any second thread of the child is ever enumerated first (or if a recycled thread id belongs to another process by the time `OpenThread` runs), the code resumes the wrong thread and the suspended main thread never starts, leaving the child hung forever while `resume` reports success. Please make this deterministic: collect all matching thread ids, close the snapshot, and fail with a typed error when the count is not exactly 1 (instead of silently `break`ing on the first hit), or obtain the primary thread handle directly during creation rather than re-discovering it by pid.

The return values of the teardown FFI calls are discarded (`libc::kill` here, `TerminateJobObject`/`CloseHandle` below), so a failed kill is completely silent: the MCP process tree can keep running (e.g. `EPERM`/`ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED`) with no diagnostic anywhere. Consider making `terminate` return a `Result<(), McpError>` so the explicit call sites can observe/report the failure, and let `Drop` discard it explicitly (`let _ = self.terminate();`) — or at minimum record the errno rather than dropping it.

The process-group id is latched here and never invalidated, and the tree keeps no handle/liveness information about the child (the child is owned elsewhere). If the tree is dropped after the child has already exited and been reaped, `kill(-pgid)` targets a pid that the OS may have recycled to an unrelated process group, killing unrelated processes. comments.content: When the reader task exits (stdout EOF) it only fails the currently-registered pending entries; it never marks the transport as closed. Any `request()` issued afterwards passes the `closed` check, inserts a new oneshot sender, writes to stdin and then awaits a response that no reader will ever deliver: the sender is still owned by the map, so `receiver.await` never resolves and the request hangs forever (same problem applies to the `Err(error)` branches and to `parse_incoming` failures below). Fix: share the closed flag with the reader (e.g. store `closed: Arc<AtomicBool>` and pass a clone into `spawn_reader`) and set it before `fail_all`, or have `request()` observe reader-task liveness.

`force_close_resources` silently skips cleanup whenever a lock is momentarily contended. The reader task holds an `Arc` clone of `writer` and `write_serialized` keeps that lock across `write_all().await`/`flush().await`, so a blocked write means `try_lock` fails here and stdin is never closed, while a leaked `Child` `/` non-aborted reader task can survive the forced shutdown/Drop path. At minimum log/report the skipped cleanup, and for the reader task store a `tokio::task::AbortHandle` (cloning/aborting it needs no lock) next to the `JoinHandle` so it can always be aborted.

Check-then-act race: `closed` is tested at the top of `request()` and the pending entry is inserted later. If `close()` sets `closed` and drains the pending map between those two points, the new sender is inserted after `fail_all` has run, so nothing will ever resolve it and `receiver.await` blocks forever instead of returning `NotReady`. Re-check `closed` while still holding the pending lock (close sets `closed` before draining, so this ordering is sufficient).

comments.content: Treating every numeric id `<=` the highest id ever issued as a benign late response silently swallows responses that were never solicited (wrong/mismatched id from a buggy or compromised server) — the only signal left is a dropped value. Consider tracking the set of recently completed ids (bounded) so that "response for an id we actually issued and already settled" is distinguished from "response for an id we never issued", and surface/log the latter as a protocol violation.

The outbound path reuses the response limit (`max_message_bytes` is set from `options.max_response_bytes`) and reports `McpError::ResponseTooLarge` for oversized client→server messages, which is misleading both in naming and in configuration: an operator tuning the response limit also silently changes the request/notification limit. Consider a distinct limit/error (e.g. `MessageTooLarge` or a direction-aware variant).

`task_support` is a required field with no `#[serde(default)]`. In the MCP schema `ToolExecution.taskSupport` is optional (defaults to `"forbidden"`), so a conforming server that sends `"execution": {}` will make the whole `tools/list` response fail to deserialize, losing the entire tool list instead of falling back to the safe default. Add a serde default mapping to `McpTaskSupport::Forbidden` (requires a `Default` impl on the enum, since `#[serde(default)]` needs `Default` on the field type).

This is security-relevant for this type: `local_effects` is keyed by name only, so `set_local_effect("foo", ReadOnly)` will also classify any *other* tool named `foo` as read-only, and `get`/`effect_for` resolve duplicates to the first/registered entry. A server (or two merged listings) publishing a duplicate name can therefore inherit the trusted read-only classification applied to another tool. Reject or deduplicate duplicate names when constructing the set (e.g. keep the first occurrence and drop/flag the rest).

Suggest accepting connections until `finish()` signals shutdown (e.g. `tokio::select!` between `listener.accept()` and a shutdown channel/`Notify`) and then asserting on the full captured set, so unexpected or missing traffic is observable.

comments.content: Internally-tagged `StopReason` cannot actually fulfill `Other`'s documented role as fallback for unknown endpoint reasons. With `#[serde(tag="type")]`, an unknown `"type":"timeout"|"foo"` fails deserialization with `unknown variant` instead of mapping to `Other`; `Other` is only reachable on explicit `"type":"other"`. To support forward-compatible providers you need a custom `Deserialize` (or `#[serde(other)]` unit fallback + separate payload) that captures the unknown tag string into `Other { reason }`.

Derived `Deserialize` for `Other { reason: String }` bypasses the documented `经脱敏并规范化` invariant: any JSON with `"type":"other"` accepts an arbitrary untrusted string (overlong, control characters, PII/secrets, non-normalized case/whitespace) without sanitization. Validate/normalize on deserialization (trim, lowercase, charset-filter, truncate to e.g. 64 chars) or make the field private with a `new()` constructor that enforces it, and document whether deserialization is trusted.

Per-field `update_from` merge can silently produce regressed/inconsistent totals: a smaller `newer` value overwrites a larger cumulative counter, and updating components without `total_tokens` (or vice versa) leaves `total != input+output` stale with no detection. Document whether snapshots are cumulative/delta and monotonic, or add a monotonic/max variant and a consistency helper.

Correctness relies on an implicit cross-crate contract that every adapter already folds cache tokens into `input_tokens`; a divergent adapter silently yields wrong or >1 rates, and `u64 as f64` loses precision past 2^53. Make the contract explicit (debug_assert + docs) and decide contradictory `cache_read > input` handling in one place instead of pushing it to every consumer.

Request-reply pairing race: `requests` and `replies` are guarded by two independent `Mutex`es with sequential `push(request)` then `pop_front()`. Concurrent `stream()` calls can interleave as push(A), push(B), pop(B), pop(A), so the order of recorded requests no longer matches the order of popped replies and the wrong `ScriptedReply` is bound to a request. Since `ModelProvider: Send+Sync`, concurrent use is allowed.

comments.content: Thread-per-wait timer does not scale and violates Future waker contract. Every BackoffSleep and every idle-gap in IdleWatchdogStream spawns a dedicated OS thread that sleeps in 50ms slices. For SSE with N deltas this creates O(N) threads (cancel+recreate per event), and under concurrent requests easily exhausts threads. Worse, poll_deadline_wait registers only the first waker (`if !*registered`) and never updates it, so task migration or a new waker is lost — the thread may wake a stale waker and the task stalls until the next spurious wake. Relaxed on the cancel flag only adds delayed visibility.
comments.suggestion_code: Prefer a shared timer wheel / executor-agnostic async timer (e.g. futures-timer, async-io) or a single shared watchdog thread. If keeping DeadlineTimer, store the latest Waker and update it on every Pending poll (e.g. via Mutex<Waker> shared with the thread), use Acquire/Release for `cancelled`, and reuse one timer per stream instead of cancel+respawn per event.

comments.content: Registration-failure fallback diverges in a dangerous way: BackoffSleep degrades to zero-wait immediate retry while IdleWatchdog degrades to immediate cut. Under thread-exhaustion (exactly when spawn fails) backoff will tight-loop retries hammering the provider, while the watchdog reports a Timeout that never actually elapsed (`is_watchdog_idle_cut` will classify it as Timeout). The `Instant::now() >= timer.deadline` check to distinguish the two cases is fragile because the deadline was just created.
comments.suggestion_code: Do not silently degrade. On spawn failure return Pending and arrange a fallback wake (e.g. yield_now + re-poll with backoff), or propagate a terminal `Transport{retryable:false}` / `StreamInterrupted{retryable:false}` with a distinct message that is not classified as Timeout. Cap consecutive zero-wait retries.

comments.content: create() holds `sessions` Mutex across filesystem and session-creation I/O (`ensure_project_storage`, `register_session_location`, `RuntimeSession::create_session`). This serializes all manager ops (get/cancel/close/list) behind potentially slow/blocking work and amplifies contention. Fix: reserve the ID with a check-then-insert of a placeholder, drop the guard to do I/O, then publish or roll back; or at minimum drop the guard before I/O and use insert-if-absent on publish to preserve the single-winner guarantee.

open() holds `sessions` guard across `session_config()`, `recover_session_mutations()` and `RuntimeSession::open_session()` — all filesystem/journal I/O. Same contention/liveness problem as create(), plus `recover_session_mutations` on shared storage can be slow. Fix: check registered set, drop guard, do recovery+open off-lock, then re-lock and insert with contains_key check to keep atomic registration.

close() calls `session.close_runtime()` while holding the manager `sessions` lock, and close_all() iterates and closes while holding it. Shutdown/cancellation work can block; any concurrent get()/cancel_turn() needing the same mutex is starved, increasing cancellation latency and risking deadlock if shutdown ever re-enters the manager. Fix: clone the target handle under lock, drop the guard, run close_runtime off-lock, then re-lock only to remove on success (close_all: collect handles, close off-lock, then sweep successes).

delete()/fork_closed_session()/prepare_edit_user_closed_session() hold the `sessions` guard across lease acquisition and delete/fork/archive filesystem transactions (`session_config`, `try_acquire`, `delete_session_storage`, `fork_session`, `prepare_edit_user`). Readers (get/active_turns) are blocked for the whole transaction; should be check-then-release-then-act: snapshot the contains_key check under lock, drop guard, do I/O, then re-validate registration before publishing location maps.

session_config() maps any `try_exists()` I/O failure to `SessionNotCreated` via `map_err(|_| ...)`, discarding permission/IO context and misleading callers (unreadable storage looks like missing session). Preserve the source error with context instead of collapsing to not-created.

comments.content: Lagged watermark uses `saturating_add` and auto-advances `last_observed_delivery_sequence` without validating tokio broadcast cursor semantics. On `u64::MAX` boundary both bounds saturate to the same value, producing an inverted/empty range. More importantly, advancing the watermark on `Lagged` means a second `recv()` without snapshot/journal replay will return buffered tail data instead of repeating the catch-up signal, allowing callers that ignore the first error to silently skip authoritative facts.

comments.content: One-shot gate relies on `Notify` permit caching. `stream()` creates `gate.notified()` lazily on first model call, while the test does `wait_until_turn_running/child_running` then `notify_one()`. Prefer an explicit one-shot (`oneshot::channel`, `watch`, or `Barrier`) for a single release.

comments.content: RootChanged/CatalogStale mapped to retryable can never succeed on this frozen Arc<SkillCatalog> snapshot: execute() clones the same catalog and retries will hit the same stale root. Retryable implies the agent should retry the same tool with the same catalog, causing a futile retry loop. Cancellation is only checked before and after `spawn_blocking().await`, so a cancelled Turn still waits for the blocking `catalog.load()` file read to finish. This delays shutdown/cancellation and holds a blocking-pool thread needlessly. Use `tokio::select!` on cancellation vs the join handle (and abort/detach the blocking task) instead of awaiting unconditionally. Also map JoinError::is_cancelled to cancelled_error() rather than generic retryable worker-failed.

The session-ID value is therefore reinterpreted as template syntax by the second stage, and conversely argument-supplied text that happens to contain argument placeholders can be double-expanded. comments.content: TodoWrite mutates runtime session state via `replace_todos` yet `effect()` returns `ToolEffect::ReadOnly`. If the scheduler trusts `ReadOnly` to enforce read-only/plan-mode write-gates, mutating calls will bypass them. Same pattern repeats for Goal (create/update/complete/block/clear) and Plan (write/clear). Return a mutating/write effect for mutating actions, or split read vs write effects.

Cancellation is checked only before `spawn_blocking`. Once the blocking `replace_todos`/`execute_goal_action`/`replace_plan` is spawned it commits even if the turn was cancelled, so a cancelled turn can still mutate Todo/Goal/Plan. This is not cancellation-safe for transactions. Check `cancellation` after the join and/or make the controller operation cancellable (abort or compensate), or document why commit-after-cancel is safe given idempotent `operation_id`.

All `spawn_blocking` JoinErrors (panic, pool shutdown, abort/cancellation) are normalized to permanent `state_task_failed`. Panics indicate bugs and pool-shutdown/abort indicate retryable resource exhaustion or cancellation, not invalid input; mapping them to `permanent` prevents retries and conflates cancellation with validation failure. Inspect `error.is_panic()/is_cancelled()` and map to `state_internal_error`/`cancelled`/`retryable` accordingly.

Empty/whitespace-only `description` is silently coerced to `Some(None)` (clear/no-op) instead of `invalid_input`. A model mistake (`\"description\": \" \"`) can unintentionally clear the goal description without an explicit `null`. `required_string`/`optional_non_null_string` reject empty after trim; `nullable_string_value` should do the same and only accept `null`/missing for clear.

`parse_todo_input` clones the whole `Value` (`from_value(input.clone())`) and then clones every `TodoItem` (`item.clone().normalized()`) plus `item.content.clone()` for duplicate detection. `execute()` already owns the `Value`, so this is 2-3x allocation. Take `Value` by value (or deserialize from `&Value` without cloning) and normalize in place without per-item clones, e.g. drain/replace or `normalized()` on owned item, and check duplicates by `&str` borrow.

Only set truncated when an additional match beyond the limit is found (like execute_glob does).

TOCTOU on size gate: file size is checked via fs::metadata before fs::read, but a file that grows concurrently can then allocate/read far beyond max_search_file_bytes. Enforce the limit again on bytes.len() after read (and skip/truncate) to bound memory.

Swallowed walk errors diverge from Glob: collect_search_files silently discards WalkBuilder errors while execute_glob counts them in errors and reports [遍历时跳过 N 个不可读取项]. Grep therefore hides unreadable paths; count/report them via skipped_unreadable for consistency.

Unbounded enumeration + full buffering: collect_search_files() materializes and sorts every walked path, then each file is loaded wholly with fs::read before max_results is consulted. A large repo (many files) or a file just under max_search_file_bytes (default 16MiB) can exhaust memory/time even when max_results is tiny. Prefer streaming the walker, applying glob/size filters before reading, and stopping early once the limit is provably reached.

Decide/document whether symlinks should be followed and make both paths agree.

comments.content: Zero-width matches are counted as hits: analyze_matches counts every regex find_iter item, including empty matches (e.g. pattern `a*` or `\b` matches at every position). This inflates Count mode, makes FilesWithMatches report files with no visible match, and creates phantom matching_lines entries for empty matches. Skip empty matches (or require match.is_empty()==false) when tallying match_count/matching_lines.

Synchronous `std::fs::*` inside many `#[tokio::test]` tasks blocks the async runtime worker thread (read/write/canonicalize/read_dir). Under parallel test execution this stalls other tasks and can mask production async-blocking issues. Prefer `tokio::fs` or `tokio::task::spawn_blocking` for setup/assertions in async tests, or switch pure-filesystem setup tests to `#[test]`.

On loaded CI (noted Windows PowerShell cold-start variance) this is both flaky (false timeout) and unsound (a delayed child writing after 1100ms yields a false pass). comments.content: Before/after process-tree diff cannot prove "no external process": blocked Shell/Git spawn short-lived children that exit during `run_turn`, so `process_snapshot()` after the turn misses them entirely (false negative). Prefer to rely on `executions==0` + filesystem/git snapshots as the sound signal, or intercept process creation (e.g. count `Command` spawns) rather than polling the live tree.

comments.content: route_client_response() stringifies both ClientRequestBridgeError and AgentRuntimeError into String, discarding the InvalidResponse vs UnknownRequest vs UnknownClientRequest/ClientResponseRejected distinction downstream needs for diagnostics, retry vs drop, and metrics. Return a typed error (or a unified enum boxing both) instead of Result<(), String>.

Non-string ids are split inconsistently: null/number -> UnknownRequest, bool/array/object -> InvalidResponse. This can pin the `tempdir` deletion, pollute later runs, and makes the lease-release assertion flaky (it only proves the `await` timed out, not that the lease was released without a lingering worker racing the next turn). Consider bounding the child lifetime (e.g. `sleep 0.5`), explicitly killing on drop, and asserting the process table/handle is reaped.

comments.content: Late-completion assertion cannot distinguish which run completed the lease. Both the cancelled first run and the reloaded second run insert the same key `("root", SessionStart)` into `started`, so `contains(...)` passes even if the stale worker overwrote the reloaded result. Combined with polling on `callback_completion_count() <= completed_before_release`, the test does not prove "late success cannot complete reloaded candidate" — it only proves *some* completion happened. Assert the completion-count delta, the owner/epoch of the completion, or that `additions[0].text == "reloaded"` was not clobbered.

comments.content: Cancelled-prompt retry changes the hook set (second registry only contains SessionStart, no UserPromptSubmit), so `additions.len()==1` trivially passes. It does not prove the lingering `UserPromptSubmit` worker cannot inject stale `prompt guidance` after the retry, nor that the retry runs SessionStart exactly once under race with `prompt-finished`. Strengthen to keep the prompt hook in the reloaded set or assert that no late prompt context is delivered after `release`.

Fail-open mapping for PreToolUse/SessionStart: invalid `permissionDecision`, unparsable JSON, and non-zero exits in SessionStart all map to `""` (non-blocking/allow). Since `SessionTurnStateRefs` is all-required, partial injection can only happen via cast/`as`, but the fallback invites it. Select atomically instead.

Host reconciliation never touches `pendingVisibleTurnBySessionRef`, so a host snapshot that moves/clears the active turn can leave a stale pending-visible entry behind. Cleanup today only happens on `first_visible_token`, turn completion, history recovery, or session-switch sweep (`useAcpRuntimeTurnMetrics`/`history.ts`/`events.ts`), leaving a window where a completed-but-uncommitted `turnId` lingers for a session whose host turn already advanced.

Exposing writable `connectingRef` alongside `connecting` state creates two sources of truth: any consumer can write `connectingRef.current` directly and bypass `setConnectingState`, desyncing the `useSessionConnection` guard (`if (connectingRef.current) return null`) from the rendered `connecting` UI state. Additionally `connecting`/`connectingRef` are always local even when turn maps are injected, so two hook instances sharing the same turn maps do not share the connect guard.

When `stateRefs.observeHostActiveTurn` is provided, the internal reconcile path is silently skipped while the (possibly local) turn maps are still returned. A caller that injects only the callback, or an external callback that closes over a different set of maps than the refs returned here, will leave consumers assuming host updates are applied to the exposed maps when they are not.

comments.content: Case-insensitive comparison is correct for Windows/macOS but wrong on case-sensitive Linux FS: `/Repo` vs `/repo` are distinct directories yet treated as equal. This can over-filter in `siblingWorktrees` (hides a distinct worktree) or return the wrong entry in `findWorktreeAt`. Consider case-sensitive comparison by default (or platform-aware / opt-in insensitive flag) and document the choice.

Allowlist is insufficient for `git check-ref-format` branch rules: it permits `..` inside (`foo..bar`), leading `.` (`.foo`), trailing `.` (`foo.`), and `.lock` suffix (`foo.lock`) which git will reject late in `worktree add -b`. Add explicit checks for `includes('..')`, leading/trailing `.`, and /\.lock$/i instead of relying only on the charset regex. Note: `@{`, `~^:?*[` are already rejected by the regex, so no change needed there.

Drive-root / filesystem-root inputs resolve to a bogus sibling: `C:/` normalizes to `C:`, so `base` becomes `C:` and result is `C:-<name>` instead of throwing. Same for bare `C:`. Validate that `main` is an absolute non-root path with a real basename (e.g. reject drive-root, require `/` or `X:/...` prefix) before deriving `<parent>/<base>-<name>`.

`refs/heads/` with empty suffix yields `branch === ''` (falsy-but-not-null) because only the else-branch applies `|| null`. Downstream `worktreeLabel` tolerates it, but the `GitWorktreeEntry` invariant (`string | null`) is broken. Use `|| null` on both branches or explicitly coerce empty to null.

Set a placeholder (`isMain:false`) in the loop and keep the final normalization as the single source of truth.

comments.content: Timer base (`base`/`startedAt`) is recomputed on every `timeUsedSeconds`/`createdAtMs`/`running` change. Since `base = max(persisted, stored)` mixes server-side accumulation with locally accumulated wall-time, restarts can double-count or drop seconds, and ticking `timeUsedSeconds` churns the interval every second. Also `current?.createdAtMs` never changes for the same id and only adds restarts. Narrow deps to `goalId`/`running` and accumulate delta since last server sync instead of resetting `startedAt`.
